candidates.title: Groomed-trail ride to the Monts-Valin snow country
candidates.summary: A short groomed-trail ride from the Saguenay side up toward Monts-Valin, which is known for deep snow and suits mixed experience. The final destination was not answered, so this is offered as an out-and-back or first leg. Two riders are complete beginners, so a guide and slower pace are worth considering. Duration not measured.

candidates.title: Groomed-trail leg toward Lac-Saint-Jean
candidates.summary: A ride west on the regional groomed network toward the lake, with villages and fuel along the way. It keeps distances within the 180 km range between stops. Riding time is not measured and conditions on the lake ice are not accounted for. Plan to stay on marked trails only.

candidates.title: Lakeshore groomed-trail leg around the lake's east side
candidates.summary: A continuation leg along the Lac-Saint-Jean shore, broken by fuel and meal stops in lakeside towns. This works if the party chooses a multi-day loop. Exact trail routing, distance and time are not checked. Access needs and ages were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidates.title: Return leg on groomed trail to the Saguenay base
candidates.summary: A leg that closes a loop back to the rental base. Rental machines usually have to go back where they started, so this matters. Distance and time depend on the route chosen and are not measured.

candidates.title: Fjord-side groomed-trail leg toward Sainte-Rose-du-Nord
candidates.summary: A shorter, scenic leg along the north side of the Saguenay fjord. It can be a gentler alternative for the two first-time riders. Trail access and grooming are not checked, and riding time is not measured.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple motel directly on or beside the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean groomed trail network suits mixed-experience riders: short, groomed legs and parking for sleds. Destination, ages and access needs were not answered, so the exact town and room setup are unconfirmed.

candidatesAccepted.title: Snowmobile-friendly auberge around Lac-Saint-Jean
candidatesAccepted.summary: Simple inns around Lac-Saint-Jean commonly cater to snowmobilers with sled parking and trail access, keeping daily distances well inside a 180 km range on groomed trail. Destination was not answered, and accessibility needs are unknown.

candidatesAccepted.title: Simple trailside lodge in the Monts-Valin area
candidatesAccepted.summary: Monts-Valin is known for deep snow and groomed trails reachable from Saguenay; a basic lodge there gives novices a scenic but manageable base. Whether the party wants this direction was not answered; confirm trail grooming status locally.

candidatesAccepted.title: Basic motel in Alma on the groomed trail network
candidatesAccepted.summary: Alma sits on main groomed trail corridors east of Lac-Saint-Jean, with simple motels used by snowmobilers, a sensible short-leg stop for beginners. Destination and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Guided snowmobile intro session for first-time riders
candidatesAccepted.summary: Two of the four have never ridden, so a short guided session on a groomed loop helps them learn throttle, braking and trail etiquette before longer days. Destination was not answered, so the operator and place are left open. Ages and access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Groomed-trail ride on the Fjord du Saguenay side
candidatesAccepted.summary: Groomed Fédération des clubs de motoneigistes du Québec (FCMQ) trails run near the Saguenay fjord, with views that suit a shorter, scenic ride for a mixed-experience group. A trail pass is required, and rental machines may include it. Exact trail conditions, distances and timing were not checked.

place.name: Saguenay Fjord area groomed snowmobile trails

candidatesAccepted.title: Lac-Saint-Jean loop trail segment
candidatesAccepted.summary: The trail network around Lac-Saint-Jean is well known and mostly groomed, and it can be ridden in parts that fit within the group's 180 km range. The destination was not answered and segment lengths were not verified.

candidatesAccepted.title: Monts-Valin snowmobile ride
candidatesAccepted.summary: The Monts-Valin area gets deep snow and has groomed trails with highland scenery, which suits the experienced pair. Confirm that the beginners are comfortable before choosing this. Conditions and trail grooming were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Rental and novice briefing at a Saguenay-area outfitter
candidatesAccepted.summary: Two riders have never ridden, so a guided orientation on rental sleds before longer groomed-trail days matters most. Rental terms, licence and insurance requirements, and the outfitter itself were not checked. Ages and access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Check FCMQ trail conditions and the trail access permit
candidatesAccepted.summary: In Québec the FCMQ (Fédération des clubs de motoneigistes du Québec) publishes trail status and sells the access permit that riding its groomed network requires. Its trail map shows which segments are open and groomed. Use it and the local clubs as the authoritative source; nothing here clears you to ride.

candidatesAccepted.title: Cold-weather riding kit for deep-winter sleds
candidatesAccepted.summary: Late January to February in Saguenay can bring extreme cold with wind chill at speed. Kit to plan for: insulated suit, a helmet with a heated or breath-box visor, balaclava, insulated boots and mitts, and spare liners. Check Environment and Climate Change Canada forecasts and warnings before each ride. Many rental outfitters rent suits, but this was not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Groomed-trail loop toward Lac-Saint-Jean, within a 180 km range
candidatesAccepted.summary: A groomed trail suits the mixed group and its stated preference for fewer kilometres on a groomed trail. Keep each leg well inside the 180 km range so a fuel stop always falls within reach. Never cross lake ice unless local clubs or officials confirm it is marked and open. Route and lodging were not checked because no destination was given.

candidatesAccepted.title: Québec snowmobile trail access permit (FCMQ droits d'accès)
candidatesAccepted.summary: Riding the groomed Trans-Québec network requires a trail access right per machine; rental outfitters often include or sell it, so confirm before paying twice. Destination not answered, so the exact trail region is unaccounted for.

place.name: Fédération des clubs de motoneigistes du Québec

candidatesAccepted.title: Snowmobile rental with guide or orientation for novices
candidatesAccepted.summary: Two riders have never driven a sled; a Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean outfitter offering a briefing or guided first day suits a groomed-trail-only plan. Check driver licence requirements and minimum age; ages were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Damage deductible and liability coverage review
candidatesAccepted.summary: Rentals carry large damage deductibles and Québec requires liability insurance on sleds; confirm what the rental includes, whether a deductible buy-down exists, and whether travel/medical cover includes snowmobiling.

candidatesAccepted.title: Connectivity and emergency plan for trail gaps
candidatesAccepted.summary: Cell coverage drops between villages on long trail stretches; consider renting a satellite messenger and carrying offline trail maps (iMotoneige). Exact route unknown since destination was not answered.

gaps.detail: This part of the plan was left out to keep the run inside its budget. Re-planning with a larger budget would fill it in.
